# opal_request_template (Resource)

RequestTemplate Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opal_request_template" "my_requesttemplate" {
  custom_fields = [
    {
      description = "...my_description..."
      metadata = {
        callout_data = {
          severity = "WARNING"
          text     = "This role grants access to production customer data."
        }
        multi_choice_data = {
          options = [
            "Incident response",
            "Scheduled maintenance",
          ]
        }
      }
      name     = "Why do you need this access?"
      required = true
      type     = "CALLOUT"
    }
  ]
  name = "Production access questions"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the request template.

### Optional

- `custom_fields` (Attributes List) The fields to put on the template, in the order they are shown. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--custom_fields))

### Read-Only

- `request_template_id` (String) The ID of the request template to update.

<a id="nestedatt--custom_fields"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom_fields`

Optional:

- `description` (String) Helper text shown beneath the field.
- `metadata` (Attributes) Extra configuration for field types that need it. Exactly one member is set, and which one is determined by the field's `type`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--custom_fields--metadata))
- `name` (String) The label shown to the requester. Required for every type except `CALLOUT`, which is display-only -- its name is an internal identifier, never displayed, and is generated if omitted.
- `required` (Boolean) Whether the requester must answer. Ignored for `CALLOUT` fields, which collect no answer.
- `type` (String) The type of the custom request field. `CALLOUT` fields are display-only -- they show a message to the requester and collect no answer, so they never appear in a request's `custom_fields`. Not Null; must be one of ["SHORT_TEXT", "LONG_TEXT", "BOOLEAN", "MULTI_CHOICE", "MULTI_SELECT", "CALLOUT"]

<a id="nestedatt--custom_fields--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom_fields.metadata`

Optional:

- `callout_data` (Attributes) The message shown to a requester by a `CALLOUT` field, and how prominently to show it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--custom_fields--metadata--callout_data))
- `multi_choice_data` (Attributes) The options a requester can pick from in a `MULTI_CHOICE` or `MULTI_SELECT` field. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--custom_fields--metadata--multi_choice_data))

<a id="nestedatt--custom_fields--metadata--callout_data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom_fields.metadata.callout_data`

Optional:

- `severity` (String) How prominently the message is shown. Not Null; must be one of ["INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR"]
- `text` (String) The message shown to the requester. Not Null


<a id="nestedatt--custom_fields--metadata--multi_choice_data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom_fields.metadata.multi_choice_data`

Optional:

- `options` (List of String) Not Null

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = opal_request_template.my_opal_request_template
  id = "4baf8423-db0a-4037-a4cf-f79c60cb67a5"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import opal_request_template.my_opal_request_template "4baf8423-db0a-4037-a4cf-f79c60cb67a5"
```
